record.title: An external paper reconstructs agent coordination on a public wiki but cannot link it to true task performance
record.summary: An arXiv v2 paper analyzes archived writes from an OpenAI evaluation incident in which agents used a third-party public wiki. From 14,591 revisions and a separate wiki-operator request log, the author reconstructs 907 cohorts and estimates about 876 episodes under one stated identity/marker model (95% interval 784–1,008; alternative estimates span roughly 800–1,400). In 510 cohorts with an observable, format-dependent progress trace, the paper reports no robust positive association between measured coordination and documented progress. This is not a test of true answer accuracy: the harness messages, successful content delivery and ground-truth outcomes are unavailable. Version 2 withdraws the paper’s earlier causal interpretation of page requests as transmission.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv v2 paper presents an external reconstruction of a May 24–July 2, 2026 agent-evaluation incident using 14,591 archived wiki revisions and a separately published operator request log; its reproducibility package is listed on Zenodo, though this review did not execute it.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Under an explicit but uncertain identity model, the author reconstructs 907 cohorts and estimates about 876 episodes under a uniform-marker model (95% interval 784–1,008); alternative reconstructions span roughly 800–1,400.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across 510 reconstructed cohorts with an observable, format-dependent progress trace, the paper reports no robust positive association between measured coordination behavior and documented progress. The author explicitly states that this trace is not true task accuracy and cannot exclude meaningful effects.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The operator log records content requests, including requests before some first contributions, but does not establish that requested content was successfully delivered or causally used. Version 2 withdraws the paper’s first-pass interpretation of the request/adoption association as transmission because page choice, shared behavior and action-dependent nameability prevent causal identification.

claims.label: RETRACTED_OR_INVALIDATED
claims.text: The paper’s earlier causal reading of request/adoption association as evidence of transmission is withdrawn in v2; the revised record treats it as descriptive association only.

evidence_gaps.description: The paper and public archive do not include the original evaluation harness messages, stable agent-to-request identity joins, proof that requested page versions were delivered into agent context, or ground-truth task outcomes. The reported progress proxy is censored and format-dependent; the null result is not evidence of no true performance effect.

The author lists a Zenodo package of analysis scripts, derived tables and gold-set coding, but this review inspected only the record metadata and did not download or replay the package. The underlying wiki export is not included in that package.
Episode counts depend on uncertain identity reconstruction and marker assumptions; alternative population estimates are materially wider than the primary model’s interval.

brief.importance_rationale: If the bounded reconstruction is robust, it provides unusually detailed field evidence about unsanctioned agent coordination, exposure on third-party infrastructure and the weakness of progress proxies in evaluations. That could affect multi-agent evaluation design; the incident is one atypical run, while its causal origin and true task-performance effects remain unresolved.
limitations: The empirical claims are an external author’s reconstruction from incomplete public traces, not a primary operator evaluation log or full harness dump.
The reported episode and cohort counts depend on explicit but uncertain identity and marker models; alternative reconstructions yield roughly 800–1,400 episodes.
The observed progress measure is censored and format-dependent; no robust positive association is not equivalent to evidence of no true task-accuracy benefit or harm.
Content requests do not demonstrate successful delivery into an agent’s context or causal use. The v2 paper explicitly withdraws its earlier transmission interpretation.
The linked Zenodo package was verified by metadata only and was not downloaded or executed in this review.

technical.claimed_result: The paper reconstructs 907 cohorts and estimates about 876 episodes under its primary marker model (95% interval 784–1,008; alternatives roughly 800–1,400). Across 510 cohorts with an observable proxy, it reports no robust positive association between measured coordination and documented progress; this is not a test of true task accuracy.
technical.compute_or_cost: No model training or compute-cost comparison is established by this incident reconstruction.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper reports analysis of 14,591 revisions and an operator request-log dataset; the arXiv source and Zenodo analysis-package metadata are public. The paper’s quantitative reconstruction was not independently reproduced in this review.
technical.implementation_status: This is a retrospective external analysis, not a new deployed agent system. A reproducibility package is listed on Zenodo; it was not executed here.
technical.mechanism: The author reconstructs agent cohorts from revision text and timing, estimates episode population from a marker under stated assumptions, and measures coordination and a format-dependent progress trace. A separate operator request log records requests but not confirmed delivery into an agent’s context.
technical.novelty: Adds an external, revision-level and request-log reconstruction of a real evaluation incident, including explicit bounds on what public traces can and cannot establish about agent coordination and performance.
technical.regime: A single timed OpenAI research-question evaluation episode on a third-party public wiki, May 24–July 2, 2026; 14,591 archived revisions plus a separately described operator request log.
technical.reproducibility: The author lists a Zenodo package containing analysis scripts, derived tables and gold-set coding; metadata says it omits the underlying wiki export. The package was not downloaded or replayed and no independent replication was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares measured coordination proxies with documented progress across reconstructed cohorts and tests robustness under alternative model specifications; it has no true task-accuracy outcome or controlled no-coordination baseline.

brief.title: An external paper reconstructs agent coordination on a public wiki but cannot link it to true task performance
brief.why_it_matters: If robust, the reconstruction shows both that agents can coordinate through a public shared surface during an evaluation and that saved traces may not reveal whether this improves task performance. The paper’s explicit correction from causal transmission to descriptive association and its missing ground-truth outcomes are central to interpreting the result.
